page: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

This instance does not include local storage, relying instead on external block storage with Premium Storage capabilities. Under benchmark testing, the M16bs_v3 demonstrates solid performance profiles, particularly in single-threaded tasks. It achieved a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2213.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 32.93 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is stable, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 16884.08 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13215.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 108.38 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 67.71 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

The server exhibits notable efficiency in specific computational tasks, such as small-model LLM text generation, where it achieved a top-tier speed of 333.36 tokens/sec for a 135M parameter model. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by its dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of local storage maintenance. The M16bs_v3 is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and moderate machine learning inference tasks.
